intro.title: AbortController & Cleanup in useEffect
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that fetches and displays user data from a mock API. You will learn how to use the AbortController API to cancel a fetch request if the component unmounts before the request completes, preventing memory leaks and errors. The core concept is implementing a cleanup function within a useEffect hook to abort ongoing asynchronous operations. You will work with React's useEffect, the fetch API, and TypeScript to create a type-safe component that handles side effects responsibly.
intro.usecase: In real applications, AbortController is essential for preventing memory leaks and race conditions when users navigate away from components that are fetching data. For example, in dashboard applications with live data updates, if a user switches between dashboard tabs while API calls are in progress, the cleanup function ensures pending requests are cancelled to avoid updating state on unmounted components. Similarly, in search interfaces with type-ahead suggestions, AbortController cancels outdated search requests as users type new characters, ensuring only the latest search results are displayed. This pattern also prevents unnecessary network traffic and improves application performance in complex UIs with dynamic filtering panels or real-time data feeds.
